newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer Q1 sales rise over last yr.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer Q1 sales rise over last yr.

text.p: British food and clothing retailer Marks & Spencer said on Thursday its clothing sales in the UK in the first quarter of the current financial year was up by nearly 10 percent.
The retail chain said its food sales in the same period were up 2.3 percent and for the months of June and July it was running 3.5 percent above last year.
The company, however, said its profits for the year could take a hit of 20 million stg on the strength of sterling.

Richard Greenbury, the chairman of M&S, told the annual general meeting that the company would benefit about 20 million stg in net profits due to the recent reduction of corporation tax to 31 percent from 33 percent in the Labour government's budget.
Marks & Spencer's share price rose five pence to 592p minutes after Greenbury announced the update on current trade.
